clue.text: Move is last of several in trick

indicators.note: the preceding pieces sit inside the word that follows, so it wraps round them

parts.note: first letter of a word meaning to evade or swindle

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is the only one kept

parts.note: rest of the word for a trick or evasion

explanation.surface: A card player's move: one card among several, played last, takes the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like card play, but 'trick' is a dodge, and the selected letter plus 'is' sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to shift or knock it out of its position, a transitive verb sense of move.

clue.text: I cope without an idol

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the short word that follows is taken away

parts.note: to cope is to manage, with the I kept
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they get by without a hero to worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AN out of I MANAGE to leave IMAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a statue or picture worshipped as a god, the biblical sense of graven idol.

clue.text: Trumpeter stirring mortals, rousing

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trumpet player whose rousing playing stirs ordinary mortals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' and 'rousing' both look like praise for the trumpeter; only the first is the signal, and 'rousing' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong, known as Satchmo, was the celebrated American jazz trumpet player and singer.

clue.text: Record supported by Republican correct? Shame

parts.note: to edit is to correct text

explanation.surface: Asking whether a record backed by a Republican is accurate, then crying shame.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' means the first piece sits on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their reputation, which is what shaming them does; both are verbs.

clue.text: Raised quote about hard set of principles

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top
about means around, so the turned word goes round the next piece

explanation.surface: Someone raised a quotation about a firm code of conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a body of moral principles guiding conduct, as in the work ethic.

clue.text: At a distance from Niagara Falls, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means reading the found letters right to left
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A tourist looking back at the falls from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far away or from a long way off, matching the adverbial phrase about distance.

clue.text: Tell of unusually absorbing time producing bean

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the rearranged letters wrap the next piece
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone describing an unusually absorbing time that resulted in a bean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell of' looks like a verb phrase about storytelling; it is just the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small pale green French kidney bean; the word also names a flute.

clue.text: Run English class in holiday location

explanation.surface: An English class running at a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a place people visit for holidays and recreation, like a seaside town.

clue.text: Perks, in brief, fine gents exploited

indicators.note: exploited means worked or manipulated, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: In short, well-dressed gentlemen took advantage of their perks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In brief' reads as 'in short'; only 'in' is the link, and 'brief' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fringe benefits are extras an employer gives beyond wages, such as a company car, commonly called perks.

clue.text: Trifling sum made from comic strip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very small amount of money
second meaning: Charles Schulz's strip featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy

explanation.surface: A cartoonist earning very little from a newspaper strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Working for a tiny wage is working for this, and it is also the title of the famous Snoopy cartoon.

clue.text: Comrade with great mansion

parts.note: ace as an adjective means excellent

explanation.surface: A friend who owns a grand mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a very large, splendid residence, the grandest kind of mansion.

clue.text: King first to believe in cures in medicinal plant books

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: start of a verb meaning cures
R for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: rest of a verb meaning cures

explanation.surface: A king who believes first in plant-based remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: R and B go inside HEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is an old treatise describing plants and their healing uses; the plural matches the clue.

clue.text: City guides on audio

indicators.note: on audio means as heard rather than as written, so the word is identified by its sound

explanation.surface: Tour guides for a city on an audio recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major city in West Yorkshire, England, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Informer admitting fraud with regret about being storyteller

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the informer word takes the next piece inside
about here means turned round, so the regret word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A grass confessing to fraud and regret, telling the story of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully and entertainingly, a teller of stories.

clue.text: Pest unfit to be cool leader

indicators.note: unfit means not in proper shape, so the letters are rearranged into better shape

explanation.surface: An irritating person deemed unsuitable to be a calm leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado beetle is a striped insect that devastates potato crops, a notorious agricultural pest.

clue.text: Play with vessel in laboratory not allowed

indicators.note: in puts the vessel word inside the laboratory word

parts.note: out as in ruled out, not permitted

explanation.surface: Playing with a beaker in the lab is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around and behave playfully, a phrasal verb matching play.

clue.text: Warder beginning to exaggerate achievement during drink

indicators.note: during means within, so the preceding pieces go inside the drink word
beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A prison guard overstating what he achieved while drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder, one of the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeater is the popular name for the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.

clue.text: Quest to get attention in school

indicators.note: in places the attention word inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A pupil seeking attention at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A search is a hunt or effort to find something, which is what a quest is.

clue.text: Good soldiers, with power at that time in land, set about difficult task

indicators.note: in places the power and time pieces inside the land word

parts.note: to land, as a bird does, is to settle

explanation.surface: Troops with power taking over a country at that time and getting to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' looks like an anagram or container signal; it belongs to the definition. 'Land' is the verb, as a bird lands.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is an idiom for tackling a hard problem boldly, starting a difficult job head-on.

clue.text: Concern caused by a very loud tune

explanation.surface: Complaints about a tune being played far too loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business that concerns someone, as in 'that is my affair'.

clue.text: Smell piece of old cloth in country

indicators.note: in places the cloth word inside the country

explanation.surface: Noticing the smell of an old rag somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, a scent, so a specific kind of the definition.

clue.text: Reminder uncovered around end of meeting

indicators.note: around means the uncovered word wraps round the selected letter
end of means only the final letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A note left after a meeting where someone was exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prompt, a small push that reminds someone to do something.

clue.text: Anxious gamble, starting east instead of west

indicators.note: the opening letter standing for one compass point is swapped for the other named point

explanation.surface: A nervous gambler deciding to head east rather than west.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious can mean keen or desperate to do something, as in anxious to please, which is eager.

clue.text: Letter from team magistrate turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the found letters read the other way
from says the letters are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A letter from a sports team to a magistrate, overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, so one example of a letter.

clue.text: Fuss, blushing about information finally embellished

indicators.note: about means the blushing word goes round the selected letter
finally means only the last letter of the preceding word is used

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced over a fuss about information that was dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorned means decorated or ornamented, so embellished is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Success whipped up mirth

indicators.note: whipped means beaten or stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A winning performance that stirred up laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped up' reads as one phrase; only 'whipped' is the signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement, a resounding success.

clue.text: Admire pace

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to think highly of

explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to esteem them, and a rate is a speed or tempo.

clue.text: Rail service tours are all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A train company whose tours go everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Eurostar runs high-speed trains through the Channel Tunnel between London and the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the cross-Channel high-speed passenger train linking London with Paris and Brussels.
